messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p95 latency spike observed for route /v1/generate (model group: text-gen-prod). Smart routing autoswitch triggered 18 reroutes in last 12m. Possible fallback oscillation. Runbook: <runbooks/redwood-routing#latency-fallback>. pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident created: P51789 — oncall: @cheng. cheng: on it. joining. collecting context — which customers impacted? any error spikes? nina: seeing increased p95 from 240ms -> 1.8s in us-west-2 and us-east-1. error rate unchanged (0.2%->0.25%). logs show a sequence: model variant A p95 high -> autoswitch to variant B -> variant B cold-start KV cache misses -> p95 stays high -> autoswitch back to A -> repeat. eli: sounds like hysteresis not applied to fallback rule. i can pull routing policy config. cheng: please paste the policy and recent decision log. deploy-bot: Deployment event: routing-policy latency-slo-fallback-v2 updated by infra-deploy at 1976543000. maria: I'm seeing the same loop — backup region failovers also in place, so when variant B degrades in us-west, requests route to us-east causing cross-region traffic spikes and then back. this likely caused the 18 reroutes. eli: config snippet from policy store:

```
policy_id: latency-slo-fallback-v2
trigger: p95 > 500ms
action: fallback_to_compatible_variant
cooldown_seconds: 0
max_fallback_attempts: 5
hysteresis: null
```

eli: note the cooldown_seconds: 0 and hysteresis null — that's the problem. cheng: confirm: cooldown=0 => immediate re-eval and could flip-flop. nina: yes. what changed recently? deploy-bot: change diff (1976543000): cooldown_seconds set from 45 -> 0 (intent: faster mitigation for real outages). author: infra-deploy. cheng: okay mitigation plan: 1) disable autoswitch for this route, 2) pin to a stable variant for serving, 3) increase cooldown/hysteresis, 4) notify customer success and affected customers. maria: taking step 1 and 2 now. executing:

```
# disable autoswitch for /v1/generate
redwoodctl routing update --route /v1/generate --autoswitch false
# pin to variant A in us-west-2
redwoodctl route set --route /v1/generate --model text-gen-prod:variant-A --region us-west-2
```

maria: autoswitch disabled, pin applied. monitoring. cheng: increasing cooldown and adding hysteresis, applying safe defaults (cooldown 60s, hysteresis 2 consecutive windows):

```
redwoodctl policy update --id latency-slo-fallback-v2 --cooldown-seconds 60 --hysteresis "2xwindow"
```

eli: policy updated. cheng: watch traces/kv-cache hit-rate for variant B — if cold-starts are root cause we should enable pre-warming or cache warmers. nina: telemetry shows KV cache miss rate drop after pin, p95 returning to ~280ms in 3m. pagerduty-bot: Incident status: acknowledged -> mitigated (partial). cheng: customer impact: CS reported two enterprise customers saw temporal latency spikes affecting sync endpoints; no data loss, retries increased. maria: notified CS with initial incident note. eli: question — why was cooldown set to 0? infra-deploy changed it in last rollout without rollout canary. nina: change was rolled with a quick rollback guard disabled. cheng: assign oncall followups: - root cause: policy cooldown/hysteresis removed + variant B cold-cache behavior - mitigation: pin, restore cooldown, add prewarming - postmortem owner: @eli - timeline + action items due EOD tomorrow - contact customers: @maria will update with summary and customer impact numbers. maria: taking customer comms. handing off oncall to @eli in 30m for cleanup. eli: taking over. i'll run a controlled experiment to simulate p95 and test hysteresis. nina: suggest adding automated test to policy rollout pipeline to prevent cooldown=0 in production. cheng: agreed. next steps logged in incident board: https://boards.redwood.internal/incidents/P51789. deploy-bot: Note: routing-policy change audit id audit-1976543000 linked. incident-bot: Incident P51789 — mitigated (autoswitch disabled, policy rollback) — please continue monitoring for 2 hours and escalate if p95 > 700ms. cheng: thanks everyone. final note: we'll include a short blameless postmortem and add an alert that flags policy changes with cooldown < 10s. nina: ack. end of thread.
